runs.text: I am pleased to submit my manuscript entitled "Contrasting Seasonal Rainfall Trends under Predominantly Stable Annual Conditions: Evidence from Trend-Free Pre-Whitening Analysis in Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, Thailand" for consideration as an Original Research Article in the Environment and Natural Resources Journal (

paragraphs.text: This study examined annual, wet-season, and dry-season rainfall trends at 12 rain-gauge stations in Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, coastal western Thailand, using daily rainfall records from 1981–2014 and a conditional Trend-Free Pre-Whitening Mann–Kendall (TFPW-MK) framework. The results show that while annual rainfall remained largely stable across the province, significant and opposing wet-season and dry-season trends emerged at several stations — most notably at station 500006, where significant wet-season drying coexisted with significant dry-season wetting despite no detectable annual trend. These findings are significant because they demonstrate that annual rainfall totals alone can conceal hydroclimatically important seasonal redistribution, a finding directly relevant to water-resource management, irrigation planning, and climate adaptation in monsoon-influenced coastal regions of Southeast Asia — a core concern of EnNRJ's scope. We believe this work will be of strong interest to the journal's readers.

Subject: Submission of Manuscript entitled "Contrasting Seasonal Rainfall Trends under Predominantly Stable Annual Conditions: Evidence from Trend-Free Pre-Whitening Analysis in Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, Thailand"

I am pleased to submit my manuscript entitled "Contrasting Seasonal Rainfall Trends under Predominantly Stable Annual Conditions: Evidence from Trend-Free Pre-Whitening Analysis in Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, Thailand" for consideration as an Original Research Article in the Environment and Natural Resources Journal (

This study examined annual, wet-season, and dry-season rainfall trends at 12 rain-gauge stations in Prachuap Khiri Khan Province, coastal western Thailand, using daily rainfall records from 1981–2014 and a conditional Trend-Free Pre-Whitening Mann–Kendall (TFPW-MK) framework. The results show that while annual rainfall remained largely stable across the province, significant and opposing wet-season and dry-season trends emerged at several stations — most notably at station 500006, where significant wet-season drying coexisted with significant dry-season wetting despite no detectable annual trend. These findings are significant because they demonstrate that annual rainfall totals alone can conceal

important seasonal redistribution, a finding directly relevant to water-resource management, irrigation planning, and climate adaptation in monsoon-influenced coastal regions of Southeast Asia — a core concern of
scope. We believe this work will be of strong interest to the journal's readers.
The manuscript has not been previously published and is not under consideration for publication elsewhere. As the sole author, I have approved the manuscript and agree with its submission to
Thank you for considering my manuscript. I look forward to your feedback.
Office of Water Management and Hydrology, Royal Irrigation Department
